thread:
carla: Heads up — getting reports from a few customers where stream connections emit a `soft_timeout` event but then stay open for ~10s before the server sends a terminal close. Customers see duplicate billing for resumed tokens when the client reconnects.

mike: ugh. do we have a reproduction? traces?

carla: yes, i grabbed one. console trace shows a heartbeat at t=0, soft_timeout at t=30s, then server sends `close: code=1001, reason='soft-deadline'` at t=40s. client immediately reconnects and resumes — server treats it as new session and charges again.

anita: can you paste the headers/flags captured? maybe there's a header we ignore in resume path.

carla: pasted snippet: ```
X-Stream-Mode: sse
X-Soft-Timeout: 1
X-Resume-Token: r_abc123
X-Quota-Key: org:42
```

mike: interesting — resume token present but our routing layer might be looking at `connection_state` not the header when deduping. iirc the policy in routing-service v3 changed semantics.

josh: i saw a PR that moved soft-timeout handling into proxy, but the proxy was returning `Connection: close` only after backlog flush, not immediately. that would leave clients in limbo.

carla: yep, proxy logs show an async flush window of 10s (config: `drain_delay_ms=10000`). so soft_timeout triggers client-side reconnect while proxy still considers session open.

sre-bot: incident 2026-03-18T22:12: deploy-rollback on staging was auto-triggered (owner: @anita)

anita: proposed short-term mitigation: make proxy set `X-Terminal-Reason: soft_deadline` and close immediately on soft_timeout when resume token present, so router can mark session terminal and avoid double-billing. toggled behind feature flag `immediate_close_on_soft_timeout`.

mike: ok but we need to consider taxing clients that rely on keepalive — some customers used soft_timeout as a hint to try recovering. if we close immediately some flows might be harder to recover.

josh: for billing safety i prefer immediate close by default; we can opt-in keepalive for known customers via routing policy. safer to avoid duplicate token acceptance.

carla: agree on billing-first. also console UX: we should surface when a soft_timeout -> terminal close path happened in the request timeline (a new event row). customers keep opening support tickets and we can't explain.

anita: telemetry ask: add tags: `soft_timeout=true`, `immediate_close=false|true`, and `resume_accepted=true|false`. can we emit those from proxy?

mike: yes, proxy can emit. but routing-service needs to consume `resume_accepted` to decide whether to mark billing as resumed or new. add metric `resume_dedupe_skipped` for cases where we accepted resume but billing would double-count.

sre-lead: note also quota interplay: if quota-tokens are decremented on reconnection before router decides resume vs new, we might leak counts. we need atomicity: either router finalizes resume acceptance before billing decrement, or billing is gated.

anita: design: 1) proxy sets terminal header and close immediately on soft_timeout when resume token present. 2) routing-service adds a single RPC `check_resume_and_claim(token)` which returns {accepted,true/false, reason}. 3) billing path only decrements tokens after accepted==true.

carla: sounds good. can we ship a kill-switch flag in console to flip `immediate_close_on_soft_timeout` per org? that will help sales/legal for sensitive customers.

mike: yes console UI already has a per-org feature flags panel. i'll add backend toggle and a small dashboard with `soft_timeout_rate`, `resume_accept_rate`, `duplicate_resume_billing_rate`.

josh: timeline? this is priority P1 for dedicated customers complaining.

anita: i'll spec the routing RPC and proxy change today, implement tomorrow, and mike will add the console toggle + dashboard. target: patch by EOD tomorrow to staging, monitor for duplicate billing drop.

dev-bot: created task INF-1248 (proxy immediate close on soft_timeout) assigned to @anita

carla: thanks everyone — please @channel if you spot anything odd after rollout. :pray:
